    Drozd's lemma: weakly positive forms have finitely many positive roots #

    A weakly positive unit form is positive on all nonzero real vectors v ≥ 0 (pos_real): on a face of the simplex where the minimum is not positive, a minimizer in the relative interior satisfies a square rational linear system with no nonzero solution of the homogeneous system (moving along a solution would reach a smaller face), so it is rational, and clearing denominators contradicts weak positivity. Comparing with the minimum on the simplex bounds the positive roots (finite_roots; Drozd, see Ringel, Tame algebras, 1.0).
